name: Silkscreen
summary: A travel poster screen-printed on camera: one opaque flat ink per squeegee pull, stepped colour bands instead of gradients, 1–3 px misregistration, condensed Big Shoulders names, and the facts printed last in a dark info band; each sample is a poster on a workbench, re-inked in a new palette.
suits: destination or product series in colourways
facts with a few big numbers

palette.use: cream stock: unprinted paper is the brightest colour (water glints, snow, beams, knock-outs)
the darkest banner ink; type on light inks
noon's sun ink: sun, route, key number (rare)
noon's near ink, also the info band
plank seams and the table's shadow side (proposed)
torn masking tape at the poster's corners (proposed)

type.units: poster units: the poster is 1000 × 1500 u, drawn at 0.96 px a unit
type.emphasis: the accent ink (a number, a route, a key value) and the scale of the condensed display

banned: halftone, line work, strokes for edges
fluorescent or translucent ink: every ink is opaque and flat
blur for depth: depth is value (light far, dark near)
parallax without paper gaps; full-rectangle screen shadows
fixed text inks on dark palettes: pick by contrast
random coloured dots on the table; 7:1 banners
risograph, ukiyo-e, woodcut or low-poly looks
copying a real poster's composition, park name, lettering or logo; naming a real agency

sources.what: Lemo-Opuscar style No. 54 "Silkscreen" (Silkscreen Travel Poster): STYLE.md, DEMO.md, style.json
